anchor.snippet: test('layered workspace and MCP replacement retain a legacy host and active PTY streams', { timeout: 40000 }, async () => {

entries.note: Use real PTY, WS, worker processes and MCP stdio against a host facade that lacks desktop actions. Prove immutable context across worker restart, unchanged invocation/PID/input, retained old streams, failed JS candidates, bounded workspace/tool crash recovery and private descriptor rejection. The separate cold-start test proves one supervisor under concurrent discovery. All processes/state belong to isolated fixtures; no live coding provider or owner session is operated.

An update can finish while an older tool worker is answering update_status. The facade replaces workers between requests, so the acceptance poll waits for both the completed job and a changed tool PID. An immediate PID assertion raced under the larger test suite; no timer or weaker process-identity assertion substitutes for observing replacement.

anchor.snippet: test('the agent context a host mints names the runtime directory its own supervisor uses', { timeout: 30000 }, async t => {

entries.note: The claim here is deliberately the DOCUMENT, not a resolution: every JS reader defaults the directory argument, so resolving this context through discovery.mjs succeeds whether or not the field is present and would pass against the KI-110 defect unchanged. What the field buys is a reader that computes nothing -- red-mcp -- and that half is proven in Rust (red/red-mcp/src/workspace.rs, a_context_without_a_runtime_directory_still_finds_the_runtime). So this asserts presence, the exact value ensureRuntime would use, and the key set supervisor.mjs:217 writes. Observed failing for its own reason twice on 2026-09-14: with the field dropped it fails on presence, and with the field present but keyed on another identity it fails on the value. frontDoor: false is load-bearing -- red-host writes its OWN context to the same filename, so a door would decide which writer this test read.
